context: Raised at the end of the 'resume marathon' session on run mrun-f77f62158255. Every figure below was read from a live CLI or from disk in this session; none is typed from memory. Four open blocks require engineer input: (1) the release directive cannot be satisfied as worded because nothing meets its own bar; (2) this branch forks a deliberate develop decision and reverting an instructed change needs permission; (3) the host is NOT reboot-safe and my own handoff doc says it is; (4) three authorities name three different 'next'.

questions.question: You directed '/bk-release any completed fully implemented and codex reviewed features or patches'. Measured in GLPNET right now, NOTHING meets that bar: develop is 2 commits ahead of main and both are docs/merge commits (7e9e7e5c restart-prep, 7bddb787 a merge PR); my branch's 20 commits over develop are docs, roadmap-sync JSON and trust keys plus a contested toolchain fork; the ONLY roadmap feature at state 'implemented' (qr-link-provisioning, WSJF 4.00) has NO spec dir on develop, a contradiction already recorded as marathon F067; no codexreview has ever been run against this branch; and PR #246 from another lane is open against develop right now. A standing peer ruling (marathon S6, ariellas 2026-08-24) also records RELEASE HELD pending quiescence. How do you want the release directive applied here?

options.label: Hold; report the bar is unmet
options.means: Cut no release. Record that the directive's own qualifier ('completed fully implemented and codex reviewed') excludes everything currently in flight, leave S6 parked, and let PR #246 land first so develop is quiescent.
options.cost: main stays 2 commits behind develop and no CalVer tag is cut today; if you intended a routine docs/chore patch release, this defers it by a session.

options.label: Cut chore patch release now
options.means: Run buildkit release from develop, cutting release/v2026.08.28.x over the 2 docs commits, tagging and back-merging.
options.cost: Races PR #246, which is open against the same branch; overrides the S6 HELD ruling without the peer lane in the loop; and ships a version whose only content is documentation.

options.label: Codexreview this branch first, then ship+release
options.means: Run /bk-codexreview against the 095 branch (codex-cli 0.149.1 IS present on this host - marathon S17), fix findings, PR into develop, then release.
options.cost: The branch diff is overwhelmingly generated JSON (a 2.4MB roadmap export, 358k lines of refusal records); an adversarial code review over that is expensive and reviews almost no code.

questions.question: This branch carries two changes that contradict develop's deliberate decision and a peer's measurement. (a) A root Directory.Build.props whose own comment claims it 'owns the language version' - false: .props is imported BEFORE the project body and loses to the 15 projects that set LangVersion=latest, which is exactly why develop moved the pin to Directory.Build.targets (that file's comment documents the measurement). (b) LangVersion latest->preview edits inside out/csharp/*.csproj, which are codeconv-GENERATED artifacts that develop's 2ae46a40 deliberately leaves alone. gavriella-glpnet measured at 2026-08-28T02:00Z that the root .targets already forces preview on every 'latest' project (dotnet msbuild -getProperty:LangVersion -> preview) and recommends the fleet DROP the per-project conversion. These were instructed changes from an earlier session of this lane, so I have not reverted them. What should happen?

options.label: Revert both
options.means: Delete the redundant root Directory.Build.props and restore the three out/csharp/*.csproj files to develop's generated content. The repo keeps exactly one pin, in Directory.Build.targets, verified by -getProperty:LangVersion.
options.cost: Reverts a change this lane was instructed to make in an earlier session; if you want a belt-and-braces .props for NEW projects that set nothing, that safety net goes away.

options.label: Keep props, revert generated
options.means: Keep Directory.Build.props as a default for projects that set no LangVersion, rewrite its comment to say .targets is authoritative, and restore only the generated out/csharp csproj files.
options.cost: Two files claim the same pin; a future reader must know the import order to predict which wins, which is the exact confusion that produced this fork.

options.label: Keep as-is
options.means: Leave both. The .targets still wins, so the build is correct either way.
options.cost: Ships a file whose documentation is provably false, and edits generated artifacts - the next codeconv regeneration silently reverts them, so the 'fix' is not durable.

questions.question: My own handoff document (RESTART-PREP-shiras-glpnet-mrun-f77f62158255.md) tells the next session 'REBOOT-SAFE: YES (bk-onrestart preflight exit 0)'. I re-ran the gate bare instead of trusting it: it exits 1. Two blocking findings - the systemd user unit's WantedBy= is EMPTY so it will never fire, and the XDG autostart fallback points at a DIFFERENT launcher (.../YNGENIOS/yngenios/scripts/fleet/post-reboot-restart.sh) than the unit, which is ariellas' 'two launchers' finding reproduced on a third host. Separately, 18 lanes are registered (not the 15 my doc claims) and 2 of them (claudesat, game_dev_demo) have NO session store yet are reported as '0 will be skipped'. A reboot right now does not reliably bring the fleet back. How do you want this handled?

options.label: Do not reboot; fix trigger
options.means: Treat exit 1 as binding. Fix WantedBy=default.target on the systemd user unit, collapse the two autostart roots to one, re-run preflight bare until it exits 0, and only then declare reboot-safe. I correct my handoff doc immediately either way.
options.cost: Delays any reboot by the time the fix takes; the fix touches a launcher that at least three lanes have independently forked, so a local fix may diverge again.

options.label: Accept risk; recover by hand
options.means: Reboot when needed and relaunch missing lanes manually with bk-onrestart.sh launch --wait-for-mounts, verifying by process count.
options.cost: Every lane that fails to come back sits idle until someone notices; the two session-less lanes will start a fresh thread that looks alive but has lost its context.

options.label: Escalate to buildkit; hold
options.means: Do not patch locally. Escalate to buildkit as the single owner of one deployed bk-onrestart capability (the feature is already specified on the glpnet roadmap at WSJF 4.20) and do not reboot until it ships.
options.cost: No ETA; the host stays un-rebootable for an unbounded period, and three forked copies keep drifting in the meantime.
